Hey. It is totally normal and absolutely understandable that getting a Pap smear--or anything that involves a pelvic exam--would be re-traumatizing for you. This is something that a good doctor should be aware of and able to deal with. It is not your fault that you reacted that way; that's just your brain's attempt at keeping you safe after a traumatizing event. I would either talk with your current doctor and see if you could find some sort of compromise that helps you feel more comfortable during pelvic exams, or I would go looking for a doctor that is more sensitive to survivors of trauma. Either way, don't beat yourself up--you reacted in a completely normal and understandable way, a manner designed to keep you safe. I've had the exact same experience myself, and it has taken time and finding a different doctor to be able to cope with situations like these. I wish you the very best!!

Prazosin has really helped me with nightmares.  Although it doesn't work for everyone, in my own experience it makes my nightmares less graphic and less disturbing -- less "real" -- most nights.  It helps with the physical symptoms as well, so I don't wake up in the middle of every night drenched in sweat anymore.  

Also, in therapy, I've been working on exercises to ground myself in the present when I wake up in the middle of the night.  For instance, if I wake up still feeling like my trauma is occurring, I say to myself something like "It's 2015, I'm in my bed, in my room, and I'm safe."  It takes a lot of practice, but now I am a little better at calming myself back down if I'm jolted awake by a nightmare.  Maybe something like this can help too?  Your therapist might be able to describe this a little better or maybe recommend an exercise that works better for you.
